positions.title: Chief Executive Officer
positions.start_date_basis: IPO prospectus and every later bio: CEO 'since October 2008'
positions.notes: Pre-IPO start (director since April 2004; Chairman April 2004 - November 2018, a board role in the board file). The 2010-2015 rosters title him 'Chief Executive Officer, Product Architect and Chairman' (no start date is given for Product Architect; the 2016 roster drops it) and his 2010 Form 3 officer title reads 'Pres, Prod Architect & Chairmn'. Still CEO in the 2026-04-30 10-K/A roster; no Item 5.02 officer change through 2026-10-02.

positions.title: Technoking of Tesla
positions.start_date_basis: 8-K Item 8.01 (2021-03-15): title changed 'Effective as of March 15, 2021', CEO position maintained
positions.notes: Held together with Chief Executive Officer; every roster since 2021-04-29 lists 'Technoking of Tesla and Chief Executive Officer'.

positions.title: Chief Technology Officer
positions.notes: Pre-IPO start (Principal Engineer, Drive Systems March 2004 - May 2005 before that, not an officer role). No 8-K covers his exit; the 2023 proxy and later bios say CTO 'from May 2005 to July 2019' and he is absent from the 2020-04-23 roster. The filings do not say whether he stayed on in a non-officer role. Rejoined Tesla as a director on 2023-05-16 (board file).

positions.title: Chief Financial Officer
positions.notes: Pre-IPO start. Retirement intention announced 2015-06-09; resigned as CFO (and principal financial and accounting officer) effective 2015-11-30 when Jason Wheeler started, staying a few months as an employee for the transition. Not in the 2016 roster.

positions.title: Chief Financial Officer
positions.start_date_basis: Form 3 date of event 2017-03-02; 8-K Item 5.02 (2017-02-24): rejoins as CFO when Wheeler's resignation takes effect after the FY2016 10-K (filed 2017-03-01); proxies say 'since March 2017'
positions.notes: Second CFO tenure. Retirement announced 2019-01-30; Kirkhorn succeeded him on 2019-03-13 and Ahuja was to continue as an advisor (non-officer). The 2019 8-K's 'apart from a 14-month gap' is shorter than the 2015-11-30 to 2017-03-02 gap (about 15 months).

positions.title: Chief Financial Officer
positions.start_date_basis: 8-K Item 5.02 (2019-03-14): appointed CFO 'on March 13, 2019' (Form 3 event date agrees)
positions.notes: Joined Tesla in March 2010 in finance roles (VP Finance, Financial Planning and Business Operations from December 2018; not an executive officer). Stepped down 2023-08-04 and stayed an employee through the end of 2023 for the transition; the 2024 proxy says he departed Tesla in December 2023.

positions.title: Master of Coin
positions.start_date_basis: 8-K Item 8.01 (2021-03-15): title changed 'Effective as of March 15, 2021', CFO position maintained
positions.notes: Held together with Chief Financial Officer; ended with the CFO role.

positions.title: Vice President, Worldwide Sales and Service
positions.start_date_basis: Form 3 date of event 2013-08-08 (officer title 'VP Service & Sales Operations'); no 8-K
positions.notes: First executive-officer stint. The bio dates the role from April 2013, but his Section 16 designation (Form 3) is 2013-08-08, used as the start. The 2015 roster (as of 2015-04-01) calls the role 'Vice President, Worldwide Service and Deliveries'. Bio: role ran 'to August 2015'; he is absent from the 2016 roster and his next role (VP, Trucks and Other Programs, not an executive officer) began January 2016. The filings do not say whether he left Tesla in the gap; end_reason is inferred (see open questions).

positions.title: President, Automotive
positions.start_date_basis: Form 3 date of event 2018-09-26 (officer title 'President, Automotive'); bios: 'since September 2018'; no 8-K
positions.notes: Promoted from VP, Trucks and Other Programs (January 2016 - September 2018), which was not an executive-officer role (absent from the 2016-2018 rosters).

positions.title: President, Tesla Heavy Trucking
positions.notes: Departed Tesla 'As of June 3, 2021' (8-K Item 5.02); not in the 2021-08-13 roster.

positions.title: Senior Vice President, Powertrain and Energy Engineering
positions.start_date_basis: Form 3 date of event 2019-10-01 (officer title 'SVP Powertrain and Energy Eng.'); bios: 'since October 2019'; no 8-K
positions.notes: Joined Tesla in March 2006 in engineering roles (not an executive officer). Resigned from Tesla effective 2024-04-14 (8-K Item 5.02, filed with the April 2024 restructuring announcement).

positions.title: Chief Accounting Officer
positions.start_date_basis: 8-K Item 5.02 (2019-03-14): appointed CAO 'on March 13, 2019' (Form 3 event date agrees)
positions.notes: Section 16 officer (Form 3) but not listed in the 2019-2023 'executive officers' rosters while only CAO. The 2023-08-07 8-K made him CFO 'in addition to his current role as Chief Accounting Officer'; later bios describe CAO as his role 'prior to his appointment as CFO' and the rosters list only CFO, but he still signs the 10-K as principal accounting officer (FY2025 10-K). Treated as current; see open questions. Earlier non-officer roles: Corporate Controller from May 2018, Assistant Corporate Controller February 2017 - May 2018.

positions.title: Chief Financial Officer
positions.notes: Succeeded Kirkhorn. Still CFO in the 2026-04-30 10-K/A roster; no later Item 5.02 change through 2026-10-02.

positions.title: Senior Vice President, Automotive

Every SCT that shows FY2018 (2019 proxy, 2020 10-K/A and proxy, 2021 10-K/A and proxy) reports Musk's Option Awards as $2,283,988,504, and no later SCT restates it. The 2025 10-K/A says the Court of Chancery granted full rescission on 2024-01-30, shareholders ratified the award at the 2024 annual meeting (2024-06-13; 8-K Item 5.07), and the court still entered a final judgment rescinding it on 2024-12-13 (Tesla appealing). The 2026 10-K/A says the Delaware Supreme Court reversed on 2025-12-19, holding the rescission improper. Musk's FY2024 SCT row is all '—', so the 2024 ratification is not reported as new compensation. All figures are recorded as printed.

2025 CEO awards. The 2025 proxy's FY2024 SCT excludes the 2025 CEO Interim Award and the 2025 CEO Performance Award (granted after fiscal 2024), and its illustrative pro forma FY2025 row (in millions) shows $87,750 for the Performance Award (preliminary estimate at the 2025-09-03 board grant) plus $26,060 for the Interim Award, total $113,810. The actual FY2025 SCT in the 2026 10-K/A reports Stock Awards of $158,359,009,867: $132,298,849,867 for the Performance Award (maximum grant-date fair value at the 2025-11-06 grant after shareholder approval) plus $26,060,160,000 for the Interim Award, which was forfeited on 2026-04-21 after the Supreme Court reinstated the 2018 award. The pro forma row is not an SCT and is not recorded as a comp row; the forfeited award stays in the FY2025 total as printed.

The 2022 10-K/A prints one extra '—' cell in the FY2021 rows of Kirkhorn and Baglino (eight cells for seven columns). Salary and total ($301,154) match the 2022 and 2023 proxies and every middle cell is '—', so the recorded values are unaffected.

Tom Zhu's FY2024 listed title is 'SVP, APAC' in the 2025 10-K/A (2025-04-30) but 'SVP, APAC and Global Vehicle Manufacturing' in the 2025 proxy (2025-09-17); his title changed in June 2025 between the two filings. Amounts are identical.

Pay-versus-performance TSR is printed to two decimals in the 2023 and 2024 proxies (e.g. 843.44, 1,263.09, 441.68, 890.97) and rounded to whole numbers in the 2025 proxy (843, 1,263, 442, 891); the peer values likewise (162.40 vs 162). This is rounding, not a restatement. CAP, average SCT and average CAP figures are identical across the three proxies.

Ahuja's second CFO start: the 2017-02-24 8-K ties it to the effectiveness of Wheeler's resignation, which was effective after the FY2016 10-K was filed (2017-03-01); the Form 3 event date is 2017-03-02 and proxies say 'since March 2017'. Recorded as 2017-03-02. The 2019 8-K describes the break as 'a 14-month gap', against roughly 15 months between 2015-11-30 and 2017-03-02.

Kirkhorn's end dates: the 8-K says he stepped down as CFO 'as of August 4' 2023 and would serve through year-end; the 2024 proxy SCT footnote says he left the officer role 'effective August 2023' and its PvP footnote says he 'departed Tesla in December 2023'. The officer tenure ends 2023-08-04; December 2023 is his employment end.

open_questions: Pay-versus-performance units: Tesla prints CEO CAP, the non-CEO NEO average SCT total and average CAP in USD millions. The loader stores whole dollars and the verifier requires every stored amount to appear in the row quote, so cap (except printed '—' = 0), non_peo_avg_sct_total and non_peo_avg_cap are null. The printed figures are in cap_as_reported / cap_usd_millions and non_peo_avg_*_as_reported / *_usd_millions. Loading them needs a units option in the loader (multiply by 1,000,000 and verify against the printed millions).

Taneja's Chief Accounting Officer title after 2023-08-04: the 8-K kept it 'in addition to' CFO and he still signs as principal accounting officer, but later bios put CAO 'prior to his appointment as CFO' and rosters show only CFO. No filing names a successor CAO. Recorded as current at medium confidence.
Straubel's exact CTO end day (bios say July 2019) and whether he stayed as an employee or advisor are not in any filing reviewed; Tesla filed no 8-K for it.

Guillen's first stint: the Form 3 dates his officer status to 2013-08-08 while the bio dates the role to April 2013; the August 2015 end day and whether he left Tesla before returning in January 2016 are not stated.
Musk's 'Product Architect' title (in the 2010-2015 rosters) has no start or end date in the filings, so it is noted under his CEO tenure rather than recorded as its own row.
No 2026 DEF 14A has been filed as of 2026-10-08 (the 2025 annual meeting was 2025-11-06), so FY2025 comp comes only from the 2026-04-30 10-K/A and there is no FY2025 pay-versus-performance row yet.

coverage.method: Summary Compensation Tables extracted from every definitive proxy filed 2019-2026 (DEF 14A 2019-04-30, 2020-05-28, 2021-08-26, 2022-06-23, 2023-04-06, 2024-04-29, 2025-09-17), the 2020-08-13 DEFA14A that re-issued the full 2020 proxy statement for the meeting rescheduled to 2020-09-22 (SCT identical to the May DEF 14A; recorded as its own appearance), and every 10-K/A Part III filing that carries an SCT (2020-04-28, 2021-04-30, 2022-05-02, 2025-04-30, 2026-04-30). No DEF 14A was filed in 2026 through 2026-10-08, and no DEFC14A/DEFR14A exists. One comp row per (filing, NEO, fiscal year). Tesla's SCT has no Pension/NQDC column. Not recorded: the 2025 proxy's illustrative pro forma FY2025 table (not an SCT) and the Apple (Tim Cook) SCTs reproduced in the 2025 proxy's Special Committee report appendix (another company's compensation). Checked: all 97 DEFA14As filed 2019-2026 (only the 2020-08-13 one carries an SCT). The preliminary PRE 14A SCTs (2019-04-19, 2021-08-13, 2022-06-10, 2024-04-17, 2025-09-05) and PvP tables (2024, 2025) match the definitive filings line for line (one footnote-spacing difference in 2025) and are not recorded separately.
FY2016 and FY2017 rows exist only where the 2019-2020 tables carry them (Musk, Straubel and Ahuja; Musk and Ahuja for 2017 in the 2020 filings). Earlier proxies were not extracted.
Every PvP table (2023, 2024 and 2025 DEF 14A; the 10-K/As carry none). One row per (filing, fiscal year); Musk is the only PEO. CAP and non-CEO averages are printed in millions (see open questions).

For every NEO: the 2010 IPO prospectus roster and bios, the executive-officer rosters in the 2014-2016, 2018-2025 proxies and the 2020-2026 10-K/As, every 8-K with Item 5.02 in the EDGAR submissions feed 2015-2026 plus the 2021-03-15 Item 8.01 title-change 8-K, each NEO's Form 3, and SCT/PvP footnotes on departures. Day precision comes from 8-K effective dates or Form 3 event dates (internal promotions with no 8-K: Guillen 2013 and 2018, Baglino 2019, Zhu 2023, Ahuja 2017); month precision from bios.
Pre-IPO officer history (Musk CEO 2008-10, Straubel CTO 2005-05, Ahuja CFO 2008-07) comes from prospectus biographies only.
